name: Basílio da Gama
credit: Portrait of José Basílio da Gama by F. Briguiet (19th century) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: José Basílio da Gama (1740–1795) was a Brazilian-born poet of the Arcadian school, born in the captaincy of Minas Gerais. He studied with the Jesuits in Rio de Janeiro, left the order when it was suppressed in the Portuguese empire, and went to Rome, where he joined the Arcadia academy under the name Termindo Sipílio.

In Lisbon he gained the protection of the Marquis of Pombal, whose government he served as an official. His blank-verse epic O Uraguai (Lisbon, 1769), in five cantos, tells the campaign of the joint Portuguese and Spanish forces against the Jesuit-led Guaraní missions under the Treaty of Madrid, and is among the foundational poems of Brazilian literature.
